chain.label: FAA oversight of National Airlines' cargo handling was inadequate
chain.trigger: The inspectors assigned to National Airlines were unaware of the airline's deficient procedures.

chain.label: National Airlines' cargo operations manual omitted manufacturer restraint data and specified incorrect restraint methods
chain.trigger: National Airlines' procedures in its cargo operations manual not only omitted required, safety-critical restraint information from the airplane manufacturer (Boeing) and the manufacturer of the main deck cargo handling system (Telair) ... but also contained incorrect and unsafe methods for restraining cargo that cannot be contained in ULDs.

chain.label: Loadmaster's training could not convey correct special-cargo restraint knowledge
chain.trigger: the effectiveness of the training is highly questionable because it would have been based on the airline's incorrect procedures

caused_by.evidence: his training was provided by National Airlines, which had developed the inadequate procedures

chain.label: Loadmaster improperly restrained the five MRAP vehicles on centerline floating pallets
chain.trigger: the loadmaster (a National Airlines employee) told them to use 24 tie-down straps to secure each M-ATV and 26 straps to secure each Cougar

caused_by.evidence: the procedures were deficient to the extent that, if followed, they could not have enabled him to properly load and restrain a special cargo load in accordance with the manufacturer and STC holder requirements
this training was deficient to the extent that it could not have provided him the knowledge and skills necessary to properly load and restrain a special cargo load
Contributing to the accident was the FAA's inadequate oversight of National Airlines' handling of special cargo loads.

chain.label: Crew and loadmaster did not recognize the previous flight's cargo shift and broken strap as a serious restraint problem
chain.trigger: “they just moved a couple inches” ... “all the ones that were keeping 'em from movin' backwards were all…loose”

caused_by.evidence: discussions between flight crewmembers and the loadmaster that the CVR captured indicated that at least some of the cargo had moved, one strap had broken, and other straps had become loose during that flight

chain.label: Tie-downs failed in overstress at rotation and the rear M-ATV broke free and translated aft through the aft pressure bulkhead
chain.trigger: the rear M-ATV moved aft, struck the E8 rack ..., penetrated the APB

caused_by.evidence: the likely reason for the aft movement of the cargo was that it was not properly restrained

although the flight crewmembers and the loadmaster were aware that the cargo moved during the previous flight, they did not recognize that this indicated a serious problem with the cargo restraint methods

chain.label: Aft center-of-gravity shift beyond the takeoff CG envelope
chain.trigger: resulting in a shift of the calculated CG from 31.7% (all MRAP vehicles in place) to 34.9%

caused_by.evidence: the rear M-ATV moved aft from its loaded location to the location of the stabilizer jackscrew

chain.label: Hydraulic systems Nos. 1 and 2 damaged and lost
chain.trigger: damaged hydraulic system No. 2, the tubing for which passes through the APB on the airplane's lower left side

caused_by.evidence: which moved aft and damaged hydraulic systems Nos. 1 and 2

chain.label: Horizontal stabilizer jackscrew and drive mechanism struck and fractured, stabilizer displaced leading-edge down
chain.trigger: The horizontal stabilizer jackscrew ... was severed on its lower end about 1.5 inches above the drive assembly.

caused_by.evidence: damage ... could result if the horizontal stabilizer's jackscrew actuator and surrounding structure were struck and damaged by an impact from the rear M-ATV

chain.label: Uncounterable nose-up pitching moment and steep uncommanded climb after liftoff
chain.trigger: a shift of the horizontal stabilizer from the set takeoff position to a 5° leading-edge-down position resulted in an inability of the available flight control surfaces to counter the resulting nose-up pitching moment

caused_by.evidence: Applying the CG shift to the simulated airplane produced results that better matched the accident airplane's final FDR data for pitch attitude
Hydraulic system failures adversely affect the functionality of the flight controls associated with each failed system
a range of fixed leading-edge-down stabilizer positions could result in the inability of the available flight control surfaces to counter the airplane's nose-up pitching moment

chain.label: Aerodynamic stall at the top of the steep climb
chain.trigger: the airplane immediately climbed steeply then descended in a manner consistent with an aerodynamic stall

caused_by.evidence: the simulated airplane exhibited a rapid pitch up leading to an aerodynamic stall that could not be countered with control inputs

chain.label: Departure from controlled flight and uncontrolled descent
chain.trigger: it reached its highest point and entered a roll to the right ... then began a rapid descent as it rolled back to the left

caused_by.evidence: The airplane's steep pitch attitude and subsequent departure from controlled flight were consistent with an aerodynamic stall.

chain.label: Airplane struck the ground beyond the departure end of runway 3 and was destroyed by impact and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: struck the ground in a nose-down and nearly wings-level attitude ... about 590 ft northeast of the departure end of runway 3

caused_by.evidence: it was not possible for the flight crew to regain pitch control of the airplane

chain.label: All seven crewmembers fatally injured
chain.trigger: All seven crewmembers—the captain, first officer, loadmaster, augmented captain and first officer, and two mechanics—died

caused_by.evidence: the airplane was destroyed from impact forces and postcrash fire
